title: If a design search only sees generic-gate numbers, does it find a worse SKY130 Pareto front?
summary: eda-noisy injected synthetic Gaussian error into the objectives a proposer sees. Here the error is measured: on the 40 MAC-engine designs, proposers search generic-gate objectives (cells, cycles, optionally cycles × depth) and are scored on SKY130-mapped area and latency from eda-sky130rung (Yosys 0.33, ABC dc2; map, pinned ORFS commit). The generic views differ from the mapped truth by RMS 0.036 (area) and 0.123 (latency) of each objective’s range, yet searching them costs within ±0.01 of hypervolume against searching the truth, and TPE’s lead over random at budget 20 is unchanged (+0.037, 95% CI +0.032 to +0.042, 200 paired seeds). iid noise at the matched level gives a similar answer; at σ = 0.2 it does cost TPE 0.012. Limits: one toy design family, one ABC script, no place and route (not sign-off), and the error objective is shared by both views.
lede: searching generic-gate objectives instead of SKY130-mapped ones (RMS error 0.036 on area, 0.123 on latency) costs within 0.01 of hypervolume on the 40 MAC-engine designs, and TPE's +0.037 lead over random at budget 20 is unchanged.
